newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico citrus farmers hope U.S. approves fumigator.
newsitem.headline: Mexico citrus farmers hope U.S. approves fumigator.

text.p: Citrus farmers in northern Mexico are awaiting official approval from the United States to use a hot air chamber that eliminates disease and insects on fruit exported to the United States.
The farmers hope using the chamber will lift the U.S. ban on fruits said to be plagued by a Mexican fruit fly.
"In the United States they just finished reviewing a hot air chamber to substitute the methylbromide," Regional Citrus Farmers Union president Gerardo Elizondo told Reuters.

From a crop of 180,000 tonnes of citrus fruits from the 1996-1997 harvest in northern Mexico, only 5,000 tonnes will be exported to Argentina, Canada and the United States. Only mandarins are exported to the United States because of phytosanitary laws that prohibit Mexican orange exports.
In the 1960s and 1970s the northern region exported about 80,000 tonnes per year of citrus products to the United States, according to Elizondo.
